learning_objective: 🎯 Understand that clothing is more than just fashion—it fulfills functional needs, provides comfort, and changes dramatically across different stages of life!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Baby clothes must be extremely soft, breathable (cotton), easy to put on/take off (using simple fasteners like snap buttons), and loose enough to allow diapers and crawling.
Children need durable, sturdy fabrics because they play hard. Clothes should allow free movement, have strong seams, and preferably have pockets. Uniforms bring a sense of equality.
For teens, clothing becomes a way to express identity and fit in with peers (fashion trends). Comfort is sometimes sacrificed for style, but self-expression is key.
The design of a garment matters. Zippers, buttons, and elastic waistbands must be placed safely (e.g., no choking hazards for babies) and allow independence (kids dressing themselves).
A good garment balances aesthetics (how beautiful it looks) with functionality (how comfortable and useful it is for the specific activity or climate).

fun_activity.title: 🧷 The Fastener Race
fun_activity.instructions: Try to button a shirt using only one hand, or try to zip a jacket with thick gloves on. This helps you understand why children and the elderly need clothes with simple, easy-to-use fasteners!

exam_tips: 📌 Always mention '100% Cotton' and 'Softness' when asked about ideal infant clothing.
📌 Be able to explain why 'durability' and 'ease of washing' are the top priorities for children's clothes.
📌 Understand that for adolescents, clothing is a major tool for peer acceptance and identity.
quick_recap: ⭐ Clothing needs change drastically from infancy to adulthood.
⭐ School uniforms help eliminate visible class differences among students.
⭐ The best clothes offer maximum comfort, safety, and ease of care.
